root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic branches: affinity or kinship, and melting or liquefaction.
root_idea.development: The kinship branch extends to marriage-based relationship and the formation of protected affinity, while the melting branch extends to heat effects, melted fat, and related derived forms.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form صَهَرَ.
Displayed under the citation-form noun صِهْرٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the passive imperfect يُصْهَرُ, describing what is in the bellies as being melted by the specified means.

senses.definition: An affinal relationship or kinship established through marriage; a relationship by marriage.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence it is paired with نسب, lineage. Classical interpretation discusses its precise scope differently, including which marriage-based relations it denotes and whether they are relations one may or may not marry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, to make someone undergo a severe or bitter oath, figuratively to “melt” him by it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction involving a hard or false oath and its threatened consequence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To burn or thoroughly cook with fire.
To affect severely by heat; of the sun or heat, to distress or pain, and to make a chameleon's back glisten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The glistening use is an application of intense heat to the body or surface described.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To season bread with melted fat, or to anoint the head or body with melted fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The applied substance is صُهَارَة or a closely related melted-fat substance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring or draw a thing near; of two parties, to draw near one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use may be transitive or describe the approach of one group to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter into affinity with a people, especially by marrying among them; to connect oneself to them through marriage, kinship, covenant, or mutual protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes forming the protected or inviolable relationship called صِهْر.
This is the intransitive or resultative counterpart of melting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To glisten under the heat of the sun.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attested application describes a back becoming bright or glistening through solar heat.
A descriptive use synonymous with cooked by roasting or frying.
A figurative idiom treats the grave as a substitute son-in-law in reference to burying daughters alive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dialectal form for a clay-and-stone reservoir or tank that holds water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is reported as a variant of صِهْرِيج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who melts fat; also a roaster, broiler, or fryer.
Melted or liquefied; substantively, melted fat.
Melted fat or what has melted from fat; also a piece of fat and, figuratively, marrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The marrow sense is reported as a figurative extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sheath or covering of the moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a lexical variant in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clay or wooden platform for household brass utensils and similar objects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This term is reported with an explicit qualification that its authority is not firmly established.
